fact: TechCabal reports that in April 2026 Nigeria's Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission subjected airtime lending services such as MTN's to new licensing and consumer-protection requirements.

TechCabal reports MTN suspended its airtime lending in April 2026 under a regulatory suspension linked to the FCCPC's new requirements, cutting the lending base to about a quarter of its first-quarter run rate and costing about 50 billion naira in first-half revenue.
